item.title: Dune Days Concert with Mojo Collins — Sat Sep 19, 5:00 PM — Jockey's Ridge State Park - Main Access and Visitor Center
item.description:
Dune Days is celebrated each year to commemorate the courage and determination of Carolista Baum, whose efforts helped protect Jockey’s Ridge from development and preserve this extraordinary landscape for generations to come.
This year, join Friends of Jockey’s Ridge for a special evening of music in honor of Dune Days featuring Mojo Collins & Special Guests!
A portion of ticket proceeds will benefit Friends of Jockey’s Ridge, helping support our mission to support, protect and promote Jockey’s Ridge State Park.
Come celebrate the legacy of Carolista Baum, enjoy an evening of live music with Mojo Collins, and support the future of the Ridge!
Tickets Required for Entry
Saturday, September 19, 2026 at 5:00 PM
Jockey’s Ridge State Park Visitor Center $40 Per Person
We hope to see you there! Limited seating is available, Get Your Tickets TODAY for a MEMORABLE night at the ridge!
For details and tickets please go to https://friendsofjockeysridge.org/dune-days/

item.title: "The Problem of Personhood:" Book talk & discussion with author Lisa Siraganian — Tue Sep 22, 5:30 PM — Smith Warehouse
item.description:
Reception with light refreshments starts at 5:15pm. Siraganian's talk starts at 5:30pm. Copies of the book will be sold at the event.
SHOULD NONHUMANS HAVE RIGHTS IN LAW AND POLITICS?
Over the last twenty-five years, the concept of per-sonhood has become central to many contentious debates. Corporations have won free speech protections, as if they were individuals. The right to life or freedom has been claimed on behalf of fetuses, trees, and elephants. The fund of human rights is spilling over into the nonhuman.
The Problem of Personhood reveals the unsettling consequences of granting rights to imagined persons, such as Sophia the robot citizen or New Zealand's Whanganui River. Synthesizing the political and phil­osophical debates on personhood and drawing on a varied cast of thinkers that includes Simone Weil, Hannah Arendt, and Dr. Seuss, Lisa Siraganian un­covers the disturbing impact of this contemporary development. A Remarkable Blend of Music, Dance and Heart It’s been years since legendary singer Omara Portuondo last entered a recording studio. Once known as the “Queen of Feeling,” her voice was celebrated throughout Cuba – until she vanished from the spotlight. But when an ambitious young record producer brings her a rare opportunity, the elusive diva must finally reckon with her past. Hailed as a “jaw-dropping, soul-stirring must see” (The Washington Post), the Tony® and GRAMMY® Award-winning BUENA VISTA SOCIAL CLUB™ is a journey through music and memory into the beating heart of Havana. A world-class company brings the story of the iconic album to thrilling life in this tale of big dreams, second chances, and music that needs no translation.

item.title: Glow n Flow @ Future Hooman — Thu Sep 24, 7:00 PM — Future Hooman
item.description:
An immersive drawing experience combining live DJ music, guided prompts, intuitive mark-making, ink, and neurographic-inspired techniques. Surrounded by neon light and a curated soundscape, participants will respond to rhythm, explore line and movement, and create without pressure or perfection. The session is designed to encourage flow, self-expression, creative confidence, and connection. No drawing experience is necessary. Come ready to listen deeply, experiment freely, and see what emerges. An intentionally intimate experience · 15 spots About the Artist Rahela Laquidara is a multidisciplinary artist, art educator, and enthusiastic instigator of creative situations. Her work spans drawing, painting, collage, printmaking, movement, performance, and immersive experiences, with a particular interest in curiosity, play, and making without knowing what something is supposed to become. She is the co-creator of Book of the Bizarre and founder of Figure, Fruit & Field.
Source: Downt

item.title: Mecklenburg's Declaration: NC's Revolutionary Presbyterians — Fri Dec 18 — Presbyterian Heritage Center
item.description:
An article published in the April 30, 1819 edition of the Raleigh Register and North Carolina Gazette proclaimed the following: “It is not probably known to many of our readers, that the citizens of Mecklenburg County, in this State, made a Declaration of Independence more than a year before Congress made theirs. The following Document on the subject has lately come to the hands of the Editor from unquestionable authority, and is published that it may go down to posterity.”
The document in question was called the Mecklenburg Declaration of Independence, and it had allegedly declared Mecklenburg “free and independent” from British rule on May 20, 1775. Of the 27 men who were said to have signed the document, almost all were Presbyterian.
But many people were confused – why were they just now hearing about this revolutionary action? The original document burned in a house fire in 1800, and the published version had been reconstructed from notes made by the clerk of the 1775 meeting.

item.title: Community Stories: Sustaining North Carolina’s Black Heritage — Fri Dec 18, 10:00 AM — Gregg Museum of Art & Design
item.description:
Community Stories: Sustaining North Carolina’s Black Heritage at the Gregg Museum of Art & Design presents a series of vignettes exploring spaces of dignity, belonging, safety, and imagination within Black communities across North Carolina. Featuring historical photographs, contemporary images, artworks from the Gregg Museum collection including a handmade guitar by Freeman Vines, and ephemera from community partners, the exhibition reflects on place, memory, creativity, and spiritual resilience across generations. Through stories of triumph and adversity, Community Stories honors the ways Black Americans have sustained and uplifted their communities through family, entrepreneurship, cultural expression, and soulful imagination, while inspiring future generations.
Source: NC Cultural Resources
